title: Paid Endorsers and Find Your ZYN
lessons: The player asks whether the people they see talking about ZYN online are paid endorsers.
The player sees ZYN's current homepage featuring winning user-submitted adventure photos under the "Find Your ZYN" banner.

text: The player asks whether the people they see talking about ZYN online are paid endorsers.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Is that guy posting about ZYN on my feed paid by you?

entry-first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: I cannot make a representation regarding an unidentified third party. ZYN's current responsibility policy states that the company does not pay social media influencers, including athletes and celebrities, to endorse its products.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: So all the internet hype is just people doing it themselves?

entry-first-4.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Some content may be unsponsored user speech. Branded social pages are separately restricted to platforms with age controls, and company advertising policy uses models aged thirty-five or older.

entry-first-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: This is somehow more legal than saying "no."

entry-first-6.speaker: COUNSEL
text: "No" would have exceeded the available evidence.

choice-first.speaker: COUNSEL
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: I respect the fact that the brand says it will not pay influencers.
Organic hype still does a lot of marketing work for you.
I do not want nicotine brands in my social feed either way.

first-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The distinction between paid endorsement and ordinary user speech matters to you. Noted.

first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Correct. Absence of compensation does not mean absence of cultural benefit to the brand.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Did you just concede a marketing point?

first-2-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: I identified a non-exclusive possibility.

first-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The brand's owned social presence is age-restricted. Your preference not to see it remains independently valid.
The player sees ZYN's current homepage featuring winning user-submitted adventure photos under the "Find Your ZYN" banner.

entry-return-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The homepage currently thanks adult participants who submitted photographs and directs visitors to view winning entries.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You just told me you do not pay influencers.

entry-return-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: A customer promotion and a paid influencer endorsement are not the same category.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: Convenient categories.

entry-return-5.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Categories are doing substantial work throughout this relationship.

choice-return.speaker: COUNSEL
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: I would rather see real customers than a celebrity pretending this is their favorite thing.
It still turns customers into brand content.
I do not want nicotine use becoming something I post as part of my identity.

return-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Your preference is for participant content over celebrity endorsement. That distinction is clear.

return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Yes. User participation can create brand material even when it is not an influencer arrangement.

return-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Then the appropriate action is not to submit. Product use does not require public brand participation.

return-3-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Finally, a terms section I can complete by doing nothing.

return-3-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Non-participation has been successfully processed.
